rationale: Righteousness exalts a nation in the A-colon; the waw then turns to וְחֶ֖סֶד (oshb:Prov.14.34, byte tier), a noun ordinarily meaning covenant-kindness, paired here with sin as a disgrace to peoples -- a pairing that coheres just when the kindness-noun carries a rarer negative sense (reproach) rather than its usual positive one, since the same spelling serves both senses in Biblical Hebrew without a distinguishing point. That lexical tension is disclosed rather than resolved.
rejected_alternative: Silently adopting the positive sense of the B-colon's noun (kindness) and calling the verse antithetic in the ordinary way was rejected: paired with sin/disgrace as its predicate, that sense would not track WEB's own rendering, so the ambiguity is disclosed instead.
